title: Checks for implicitly concatenated strings on a single line.
summary: While it is valid Python syntax to concatenate multiple string or byte literals implicitly (via whitespace delimiters), it is unnecessary and negatively affects code readability. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-implicit-str-concat and made it stable in v0.0.201.
message_templates: Implicitly concatenated string literals on one line

title: Checks for implicitly concatenated strings that span multiple lines.
summary: For string literals that wrap across multiple lines, PEP 8 recommends the use of implicit string concatenation within parentheses instead of using a backslash for line continuation, as the former is more readable than the latter. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-implicit-str-concat and made it stable in v0.0.201.
message_templates: Implicitly concatenated string literals over multiple lines

title: Checks for string literals that are explicitly concatenated (using the + operator).
summary: For string literals that wrap across multiple lines, implicit string concatenation within parentheses is preferred over explicit concatenation using the + operator, as the former is more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-implicit-str-concat and made it stable in v0.0.201.
message_templates: Explicitly concatenated string should be implicitly concatenated

title: Checks for implicitly concatenated strings inside list, tuple, and set literals.
summary: In collection literals, implicit string concatenation is often the result of a missing comma between elements, which can silently merge items together. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-implicit-str-concat and made it stable in 0.16.0.
message_templates: Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection

title: Operation doesn't work on directories.
summary: A subclass of OSError, Exception, BaseException.
